subject.title: [Bug]: Possible repeated Codex Apps plugin discovery causing excessive disk I/O during a single request (investigated with opensnoop and atop)

question: Should maintainers adopt, replace, or close the still-open cache proposal after current-main profiling establishes whether OpenClaw or the Codex app-server owns the repeated plugin discovery?
rationale: The reporter still observes an availability failure, while the proposed cache has not merged and source/dependency inspection was unavailable; choosing the permanent owner and cache-invalidation contract requires maintainer judgment.

options.title: Profile before adopting
options.body: Reproduce on current main and choose the narrow owner-bound fix only after the trace identifies the repeated inventory caller.

options.title: Revive the linked PR
options.body: Ask its author to rebase, provide real before/after profiling, and resolve cache invalidation and compatibility questions.

options.title: Route upstream
options.body: If profiling shows the vendor Codex app-server alone repeatedly scans unchanged plugin metadata, file an upstream Codex report with a minimal trace.

recommendation.title: Profile before adopting
recommendation.body: Reproduce on current main and choose the narrow owner-bound fix only after the trace identifies the repeated inventory caller.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the linked implementation candidate and are the only concrete person connected to the proposed remediation in the supplied record.
